fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Sky Clock From Aries to Pisces", "body": "While grabbing 52 screenshots, Chance noticed the first two acts trace a clear journey from Aries to Pisces. The library beheading opens in Aries, the Ancient One's fans point to Venus-ruled Taurus, the boastful surgeon is mercurial Gemini, his sports car is the Cancer chariot before the crash, and his tantrum is Leo. Christine Palmer plays Virgo, Kathmandu is Libra, the mugging is Scorpio, tea with the Ancient One is Sagittarius, the underworld trip is Capricorn, the sling ring is Aquarius and his sleep study is Pisces. Chance wonders whether this is what Joseph Campbell was seeing in the hero's journey."}, {"title": "Strange as a Mirror of Aleister Crowley", "body": "The episode title plays on Jekyll and Hyde, and the hosts stress they are not claiming a one to one match. Chance links Strange's obsession with reputation to Crowley's polarising name, and the hosts hear Crowley's Book 77, Liber Oz, in the surgeon's insistence that a song is from 1977. Gabe ties the Ancient One stranding Strange in the Himalayas to the story of Crowley the mountaineer, who allegedly left his party before an avalanche. The sanctum fight and the fall down the stairs recall the Battle of Blythe Road with the Golden Dawn, and the closing reading ties the ending to Crowley's claimed contact with Aiwass."}, {"title": "Healing the Hands by Surrendering the Ego", "body": "Strange begins as a hyper materialistic surgeon who turns down cases for fear that failure will stain his reputation, and the crash that wrecks his hands leaves him, in Chance's reading, a divided man. Chance treats the hands as a fractal microcosm of the whole self, echoed in the trip where fingers sprout hands. On the mountain Strange overthinks until he surrenders, and the hosts unpack the Ancient One's line that you cannot beat a river into submission. Chance compares it to dancing and qigong and reframes surrender as a shift from control to intent, while a fellow panelist draws on his own Wim Hof breathing practice."}, {"title": "Natural Time Versus Clock Time", "body": "Bells, Strange's drawer of spinning watches and his smashed watch after the mugging all mark time as a controlling force, and Chance reads the bells as a nod to Baal and to the bill that comes due. When Kaecilius says time is the enemy of us all, Chance separates two things English calls time: natural time, the cycles of nature and change that let each life grow uniquely, and Kronos time, the repeating workweek rat race. He argues the only real time is spiritual development. The finale, where Strange traps Dormammu in an endless loop with the Eye of Agamotto, reads to him as an artificial Kronos time loop."}, {"title": "The Ancient One as a Terrible Mother", "body": "Chance sees the Ancient One, whose name he reads as Tao and Tau, as more complex than a kindly teacher. He reads her fans through Dylan Saccoccio's writing as tools of Venusian purification, and ties her Celtic origin to Michael Tsarion's Irish Origins of Civilization and the idea that Eastern wisdom first came from a northern homeland. Because druid is said to mean door, he hears Dormammu as the door to darkness, and he casts her as a terrible goddess who draws on the Dark Dimension to stay immortal while withholding the full truth from her students. Another panelist compares her to the goddess Cybele."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: For this month's Marvel movie, our heroes scrutinize the sorcerer supreme, exploring the 2016 film "Dr. Strange." What does the master of the mystic arts have in common with the "Great Beast" Aleister Crowley? What's up with this multiverse meme that seems to be everywhere right now? And what occulted truths about the fractal of life are casually planted throughout this psychedelic screenplay?
